US President Donald Trump used his 2026 address to the United Nations General Assembly to portray the United States as stronger and more powerful under his administration, while defending military action against Iran, warning Tehran over its nuclear programme and claiming progress in ending several international conflicts. The 81st UN General Assembly’s high-level general debate began on September 22 in New York.
‘America is back’
Opening his address, Trump declared, “America is back -- and our country is stronger today than ever before.”
He contrasted the current state of the US with the situation two years earlier, saying, “Two years ago, our country was dead. Now, we have the hottest country anywhere in the world.”
Trump also reiterated several claims about the US economy and domestic situation. He said America was “leading in all sectors”, household incomes had increased, and the country had “the most secure border in the world”. He said illegal migration had been stopped, crime had fallen by 27%, and the US remained “No. 1 in tech”.
Trump also pointed to financial markets, saying the “American share market has made records” and that “Our money was being taken by the world”.
Iran and the nuclear issue
A major part of the address focused on Iran. Trump described Iran as the “number one sponsor of terror” and said he had remained committed to preventing Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.
“From the first day I entered the political arena, I have been unwavering -- I will never allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon,” Trump said.
He referred to the September 11 attacks in the US and the October 7 attack in Israel while warning about the consequences of Iran acquiring nuclear capabilities. Trump said the US had given Iran opportunities to reach an agreement before taking military action.
“After giving Iran every chance for a deal, I took action to ensure that neither the United States, nor any nation in this hall, would ever have to face such a nightmare,” he said.
Trump then presented what he described as a choice between a negotiated settlement and further military action.
“I have a big decision to make,” he said, asking whether there would be a deal that allowed Iran to rebuild or whether he should “annihilate the Islamic Republic” and “drive them into hell”.
He also said the US could “annihilate Iran quickly” if necessary.
Iran deal and US midterm elections
Trump said he expected a deal with Iran after the US election, arguing that Tehran was waiting to see how Republicans perform in the midterm elections.
“I believe we'll make a deal right after the election, because it doesn't make sense for them not to,” Trump said.
He stressed that he would not himself be contesting the midterms. “I’m not running in the midterms,” he said, adding that he had already won the presidency “in a giant landslide” and would remain in office for another two and a half years.
Trump also said the election would not determine his approach to Iran, saying the key issue was that “Iran will never have a nuclear weapon”.
Munitions and economic pressure
Trump rejected claims that the US was running low on ammunition, calling them “fake news”.
“We have a lot of ammunition,” he said, adding that the US was increasing production. He said 18 large munitions plants were currently under rapid construction.
Trump also called on other countries to join the US in imposing “complete economic isolation of Iran” until Tehran stops attacks on commercial shipping, abandons its nuclear ambitions and ends its support for terrorism.
He said the UN Security Council had overwhelmingly passed a resolution condemning Iran’s attacks on commercial shipping and urged countries to maintain pressure on Tehran.
Gaza and claims of ending wars
Trump also used the address to highlight his administration’s role in the Gaza conflict.
“One year ago when I addressed the great leaders in this Grand Hall, the War in Gaza was still raging brutally,” Trump said, adding that there had been “no end in sight”.
He said subsequent efforts had changed the situation and claimed, “A few weeks later, we ENDED the War in Gaza, saving untold thousands of lives.” Trump also said all remaining hostages, both living and dead, had been brought home.
Trump said that since taking office, he had “settle[d] eight wars”, naming Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Pakistan and India, Armenia and Azerbaijan, as well as Gaza among the conflicts he cited.
“While others have talked, I have acted. While others have spoken of peace, I have made peace. While others have ignored threats, I have confronted them,” Trump said.
Oil prices and US power
Trump also predicted a sharp decline in oil prices, saying, “oil prices will soon come plummeting down.” His comments came as the Iran conflict continued to affect energy markets and remained a major focus of the UN gathering.
On the broader US role in the Western Hemisphere, Trump issued another warning: “The United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere -- and if necessary, we will use our unmatched military might to secure the vital national interests of the United States.”
Trump's address came as the Iran war remained central to his UN agenda, with the president seeking to defend the US military campaign while simultaneously presenting himself as a peacemaker.
